newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communist Duma boss says Yeltsin still in charge.
newsitem.headline: Communist Duma boss says Yeltsin still in charge.

text.p: Gennady Seleznyov, the communist speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, said on Monday that Russia's ailing President Boris Yeltsin had not relinquished his grip on power.

"Despite his illness, he is in control of the situation and is taking decisions by himself. I think he has information on eveything going on in the country," Seleznyov told reporters after a 30-minute meeting with Yeltsin, who is preparing for heart surgery.
"It was not a 30-minute monologue by me but a dialogue. Yeltsin spoke without briefing papers and reacted in a lively way during our conversation."
Seleznyov, whose Communist Party is the largest single faction in the Duma, suggested last month that Yeltsin should step down if his health was too poor to allow him to work properly.
He said on Monday that the president had expressed concern about cash shortages in the Far North and in the army, where many soldiers have not been paid for months.
The two men met at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow. Yeltsin is resting there while doctors get him ready for the operation, which is due to take place in mid-November.
Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and he said on September 5 he would undergo open heart surgery.
The announcement sparked an increasingly bitter Kremlin power struggle which Yeltsin tried to end last Thursday when he sacked security chief Alexander Lebed.
"It was a case when the views of the president and a majority of Duma members coincided," Seleznyov quoted Yeltsin as saying.
